prompt: Use an ArrayDeque as a stack to check that every ( ) [ ] { } in a string is properly nested and matched. Non-bracket characters are ignored.
explanation: A stack mirrors bracket nesting exactly: the most recently opened bracket must be the first one closed, which is last-in-first-out. Push each opener; on a closer, an empty stack or a popped opener of the wrong kind means the string is unbalanced. After the loop the stack must be empty, otherwise some opener was never closed -- forgetting that final check is the classic bug.
hints: Push '(' '[' '{' onto an ArrayDeque<Character> with push; handle closers in an else-if.
On a closing bracket: if the stack is empty, or pop() returns the wrong kind of opener, return false.
Do not return true inside the loop -- after the loop, the string is balanced only if the stack is empty.
